chunks: From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) one day enter the Sacred Mosque during the Asr prayer. When the rows were bowing, he bowed alone, and prostrated the two prostrations, then stood up and continued until he joined the rows.
ai.seo_question: How did the Imam join the congregational prayer when he arrived after the bowing had begun?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam Al-Sadiq’s (AS) adherence to the Hanafi-leaning view of *Qada* (compensating for missed pillars) by performing only the bowing and two prostrations he missed, rather than restarting the prayer. It serves as a key evidence in Shia jurisprudence for the validity of joining a congregational prayer at any stage, provided the essential components are completed individually before rejoining the Imam. This incident underscores the flexibility in prayer mechanics while maintaining the spiritual unity of the congregation.
